newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sending aid troops to Rwanda - Perry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sending aid troops to Rwanda - Perry.

text.p: The United States has changed plans to send security troops to Zaire and instead will provide fewer than 1,000 military logistics personnel to aid refugees in Rwanda, U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Tuesday.

Perry said that the situation in central Africa remained fluid and, while a Canadian-led multinational force would now operate chiefly in Rwanda, Washington was ready to send protective troops to Zaire if necessary.

"There have been more than 500,000 refugees that have peacefully returned to Rwanda in the last few days. This is a very positive development and we are modifying our plans based on this dramatic change," Perry said after a speech.
He said the United States still planned to take part in the U.N.-authorized military operation led by Canada to support the voluntary repatriation of refugees into Rwanda.

"This force will require considerably fewer troops than originally envisioned and will operate chiefly in Rwanda," he said. "Our current thinking is that U.S. contribution to this effort will be less than 1,000 troops. And these will be support logistics troops rather than combat troops."

Meanwhile, Perry said, the U.S. military had already moved Air Force teams into Kigali in Rwanda, Mombasa in Kenya and Entebbe in Uganda to facilitate the movement of personnel and humanitarian aid into Rwanda.
